description:
Fix ISS-018: move reviews.db from a cwd-relative default to a stable per-user, project-keyed location so the CLI cross-provider guard works from any directory. A draft plan for this was reviewed by both providers (verdicts: revise) — findings preserved in note N-003 and folded into the steps below. Read N-003 before starting.

## Current shape
`reviewDbPath()` in `src/storage/db.ts` (~line 22): `process.env.REVIEW_BRIDGE_DB ?? 'reviews.db'`, resolved to absolute against cwd; `':memory:'` passes through untouched. The MCP server opens read-write from the project root; the CLI opens read-only from wherever the user happens to be — when cwds differ the CLI finds no file and the ISS-017 cross-provider guard silently no-ops (fails open). The file comment at db.ts lines 16-21 documents this exact deferral.

## Decision already made in triage — implement, don't re-litigate
Per-user data dir with a PROJECT-KEYED subdirectory (NOT one flat global db — that would collide sessions across projects and merge review history):
`<dataDir>/codex-claude-bridge/projects/<projectKey>/reviews.db`
- dataDir: macOS `~/Library/Application Support`, Linux `$XDG_DATA_HOME` else `~/.local/share`, win32 `%APPDATA%` (`process.env.APPDATA`, fall back to homedir). Small helper + tests; no new dependency.
- projectKey: sha256 hex (first 16 chars) of the project root path. Project root = nearest ancestor of cwd containing `.git` or `.reviewbridge.json` (same walk-up rule as `loadConfig()` in src/config/loader.ts ~line 140 — extract/share that walk, but remember: config layer must not import storage and vice versa; put a tiny shared fs-walk util in `src/utils/` if needed). No project root found → use resolved cwd itself as the key input.
- `REVIEW_BRIDGE_DB` env STILL overrides everything, and `':memory:'` stays special — both behaviors are load-bearing for tests.

## Migration of an existing project-local reviews.db (the dangerous part)
N-003 finding 1 is CRITICAL: the db runs WAL, so recent committed transactions live in `reviews.db-wal`. A bare file copy CAN LOSE DATA. Migrate via sqlite itself:
1. If `<projectRoot>/reviews.db` exists AND the new stable path does not: open the legacy db read-write with better-sqlite3 and run `VACUUM INTO '<newPath>'` (folds WAL into a single consistent file). Do NOT fs.copyFile. Do NOT migrate `-wal`/`-shm` sidecars — VACUUM INTO makes them irrelevant.
2. `fs.mkdirSync(dirname(newPath), { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 })` BEFORE the VACUUM (N-003 finding 2 — missing parent crashes at startup). After creation, `fs.chmodSync(newPath, 0o600)` (finding 5 — the db holds diffs and review content).
3. Zero-byte or unopenable existing target at the new path (finding 6): treat as absent — rename it aside (`reviews.db.corrupt-<mtimeMs>`) and proceed.
4. Leave the legacy file in place (read-only fallback semantics unchanged elsewhere); log one stderr line: `[codex-bridge] migrated review history to <newPath>`.
5. Migration failure (locked legacy db, disk full): warn on stderr and fall back to the legacy cwd-relative path for this process — never crash the server over history relocation.

## Tests (TDD; colocated; mock nothing internal — use real temp dirs via `fs.mkdtempSync`)
- dataDir helper per-platform (drive via injected `process.platform`/env, the codebase prefers injected seams).
- projectKey stability (same root → same key; different roots → different keys).
- Migration: create a legacy db WITH uncheckpointed WAL content (write rows, do NOT close cleanly / skip checkpoint), migrate, assert ALL rows present at the new path. This is the regression test for N-003 finding 1 — it must exist.
- mkdir-p, permissions (skip perm asserts on win32), corrupt-target handling, REVIEW_BRIDGE_DB override, ':memory:'.
- Update `src/storage/db.ts` doc comment (lines 12-21) — it currently documents the deferral this ticket removes.

## Acceptance
- Full gate green. Existing storage/session/guard tests keep passing (they set REVIEW_BRIDGE_DB — that override must keep working).
- Live: run the MCP server from the repo root, then `node dist/index.js review-history` from an UNRELATED directory → history visible and the cross-provider guard active (the ISS-018 repro, now passing).
- Resolves ISS-018; archive note N-003 (status archived) with a pointer to this ticket.

## Conventions
TypeScript strict, no `any`; Result<T> over throws; ESM `.js` suffixes; kebab-case files; no AI names in commits.
title: Stable per-user reviews.db location with project-keyed scoping and safe migration (ISS-018)
